key_insight: LLM-discovered heuristics directly construct promising vehicle-routing subproblems, matching neural selection policies in-distribution and outperforming them on large-scale out-of-distribution instances.
engineering_relevance: Interpretable, generalizable subproblem construction could help logistics optimization systems tackle large capacitated vehicle routing problems.
method: Use an LLM to autonomously refine subproblem-construction heuristics.
Apply the discovered heuristics to identify promising portions of a large routing problem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparable in-distribution performance and better out-of-distribution performance than neural network-based policies, but gives no numerical results or benchmark sizes.
watch_item: Deployment requires validating runtime costs and solution quality on operational routing constraints beyond the evaluated CVRP instances.
paper_title: Revisiting Learning to Delegate: LLM Discovered Heuristics for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing
